items.title: 69537_Jimmy Jones oral history interview
items.q: There was one named Bob Hawk.

ctx.x: Well, did you get around as a teenager to hear much music in Chicago? Were you aware of who all was playing while you were in your teens?

Well, not so -- yes, I did, by record. There were disc jockeys there. There was one named Bob Hawk. I don't know whether he's around now or not, and he used to play Ellington quite a bit. And he played Lunceford. And there was a fellow that played piano. His name was Dick Baker, Two Ton Baker.
